newsitem.title: FINLAND: METAL UNION'S LUNDH SAYS FINLAND SHOULD JOIN EMU.
newsitem.headline: METAL UNION'S LUNDH SAYS FINLAND SHOULD JOIN EMU.

text.p: Finnish metal workers' union chairman Per-Erik Lundh said at the weekend that Finland should join the third stage European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"If EMU comes true, Finland should be part of it from the beginning," Lundh said in the text of a prepared speech.

"It is more likely that Finland will become a member of EMU than remain outside," he said, adding that even outside, Finland would probably have to implement decisions made by the countries inside the single currency.
"We must put the country in so called EMU-shape," Lundh said. Economic and monetary union would not require lower wages or further cuts in unemployment or other social security benefits, he said.
Preparations for EMU should include a national budget in surplus, a current account in surplus and corporate equity to assets ratios above 40 percent.
"Achieving a state budget surplus will require strong decisions on growth and tools for growth. The growth that is now well under way should be fuelled by new decisions promoting growth," Lundh said.
He repeated his call for rapid decisions to make Finland a self-sufficient energy producer. Lundh has earlier said Finland should build more nuclear power.
